objectives.goal: Distinguish liking from knowing how, including person and negative ability forms.
Use dative experiencers with unchanged patinka, including friend nouns and groups.
Contrast patinka's nominative, affirmative accusative objects, negative genitive objects and listening's genitive.
objectives.limit: New-context checks sample negative objects and listening; patinka versus mėgstu noun forms have repeated retrieval, not a new noun check.

objectives.goal: Distinguish past, present and future while keeping person and location unchanged.
objectives.limit: The core contrast is explicit; one reserved check samples first-person past at a different location.

objectives.goal: Use past person endings in the -o and -ė patterns.
Recognize and use the skaitė/skaičiau stem change with the correct person.
objectives.limit: Explicit t→č contrast; wider d→dž examples remain in the retained scaffold and do not establish general productive mastery.

objectives.goal: Use future person forms for being, walking and travelling by vehicle.
Distinguish singular/plural and masculine/feminine companions after su.
objectives.limit: Named-person endings remain in retained examples; these checks sample draugas/draugė rather than every instrumental class.

objectives.goal: Give destination, quantity and travel day; ask about availability, discounts and return tickets.
objectives.limit: Core transaction is choice-based. Availability, discounts and return journeys use bounded phrases and supported construction.

objectives.goal: Read a ticket and distinguish row from seat, with feminine ordinal forms.
objectives.limit: Repeated form retrieval and visible-ticket comprehension; no independent transfer claim for all ordinals.

objectives.goal: Distinguish departure from arrival and read trip timing, platform and return information.
objectives.limit: Bounded retrieval and supported reading; reading glosses introduce incidental postcard wording without awarding its production.

objectives.goal: Recognize travel wishes and choose an appropriate reply.
objectives.limit: Prepared social phrases, not spontaneous interaction.

objectives.goal: Write a short postcard with past travel, present location and a future plan.
objectives.limit: Saved and self-reviewed; no automated grammar or communicative-success assessment.

steps.title: Choose an activity · 1
steps.note: Use infinitives to name activities. Combine them with mėgstu (I like), moku (I know how), and noriu (I want).

steps.correction: Compare the pairs in the example.

lessons.title: Enjoying something or knowing how
lessons.goal: Keep the activity the same and change liking to ability.

steps.title: The same activity, different messages
steps.note: Mėgstu describes liking; moku describes knowing how. Plaukti stays in its infinitive form after both verbs. Enjoying an activity and knowing how to do it are different claims.

steps.title: Knowing how—or not
pairs: I do not know how to swim.
steps.note: Add ne- to negate moku: nemoku. This does not mean you dislike swimming; it means you do not know how.

options: I do not know how to swim.
answers: I do not know how to swim.

steps.translation: I do not know how to swim.

lessons.title: Who likes reading
lessons.goal: Change the person while keeping patinka and the activity unchanged.

steps.title: The person changes; patinka stays
steps.note: With patinka, say who experiences the liking using man, tau or jai. Patinka does not change for these people. Compare aš mėgstu with man patinka: the person has a different form.

steps.correction: With patinka, use jai for she.
With patinka, use tau for you.

lessons.goal: Recall counting, a how-many question and a polite request.

lessons.title: Two ways to like music
lessons.goal: Compare the same person and noun with patinka and mėgstu.

steps.title: Music
steps.note: Start with the naming form muzika. Its sentence form depends on the verb.

steps.title: Same meaning, different construction
steps.note: Patinka uses the naming form muzika, with the experiencer man. Mėgstu takes an object: muziką, with the subject aš. Both sentences express liking music.

steps.correction: After patinka, music is in its naming form: muzika.
After mėgstu, the object is muziką.
The naming form with patinka: muzika.

lessons.title: Liking music—or not
lessons.goal: Keep the object the same and change an affirmative verb to a negative one.

steps.title: Negation changes the object form
steps.note: Negate the verb with ne-. The object changes from accusative muziką to genitive muzikos. This contrasts a real grammatical form, not just spelling.

steps.correction: The negative verb takes genitive muzikos.

lessons.title: Yesterday, today, tomorrow
lessons.goal: Locate an event in time before changing its verb.

steps.title: Three points in time
steps.note: These words locate an event before, on or after today. Next, keep the person and place the same and change the verb to match that time.

lessons.title: The same person at three times
lessons.goal: Keep I and Kaunas unchanged; distinguish was, am and will be.

steps.title: Only the time changes
pairs: Tomorrow I will be in Kaunas.
steps.note: Buvau is past, esu is present and būsiu is future. Kaune stays the same location. Each verb already identifies I, so a separate aš is optional.

steps.translation: Tomorrow I will be in Kaunas.
Tomorrow I will be in Kaunas.

lessons.title: Ask about tomorrow’s journey
lessons.goal: Change the person while keeping the journey the same.

steps.title: From present travel to a plan
steps.note: Važiuoju is present; važiuosiu is future. The future uses an s before the person ending, also seen in būsiu.

steps.translation: Tomorrow I will travel to Kaunas.

steps.title: I, we and polite you
pairs: You will travel to Kaunas. (polite or plural)
steps.note: Keep the future s and change the ending: -iu for I, -ime for we, -ite for you politely or a group. In a question, kur asks where; kada asks when.

lessons.title: Ask for one ticket or two
lessons.goal: Use the object forms in a polite request.

steps.title: The tickets you request
steps.note: A request uses object forms: vieną bilietą or du bilietus. The question kiek takes genitive plural bilietų, just like kiek kambarių in the previous chapter.

steps.correction: Du asks for two; vieną asks for one.

lessons.title: State the destination and day

steps.title: To or from the same city
steps.note: Į identifies the destination and takes Kauną. Iš identifies the origin and takes Kauno. The city is the same; the direction is different.

steps.title: Where and when
steps.note: Važiuosite addresses the customer politely. Kur asks for the destination; kada asks for the time. These questions use the future form you have practised.

steps.correction: Kada asks when; kur asks where.

lessons.goal: Keep the past time and place; change only the person.

steps.title: I, you and she
steps.note: The past stem is buv-. Add -au for I, -ai for informal you and -o for he/she. The place does not change.

steps.title: We and polite you
pairs: You were in Kaunas. (polite or plural)
steps.note: Use -ome for we and -ote for polite/plural you. With jie or jos (they), use the same buvo as with jis or ji.

lessons.title: Report a journey
lessons.goal: Transfer the familiar past-person endings to travelled.

steps.title: The same journey, different people
steps.note: Keliauti means to travel. The past stem keliav- uses the same -au / -ai / -o endings as buv-. Learn the stem with the verb; not every past stem is predictable from its infinitive.

steps.title: More than one traveller
steps.note: The plural endings match buvome / buvote: keliavome / keliavote.

lessons.title: A different past-tense pattern
lessons.goal: Keep the eating action fixed to learn the -ė pattern.

steps.title: I, you and she ate

steps.title: A student discount
steps.note: Studentams means for students. Learn this useful request as a phrase; the plural dative pattern is not assessed here.

steps.title: The trip and the next plan
pairs: Tomorrow we will travel by train.
steps.note: Važiavome is the past we form, following the -ome pattern in keliavome. Važiuosime is the future. Traukiniu stays the means of travel in both.

steps.correction: Past we travelled by vehicle: važiavome.

steps.translation: Tomorrow we will travel by train.

steps.title: Arriving and returning
steps.note: Atvykome is the past we form of atvykti, to arrive. Grįšime is the future we form of grįžti, to return; notice ž becomes š before the future ending. Learn this changed stem explicitly.

steps.title: Departure versus arrival
steps.note: Išvyksta means departs; atvyksta means arrives. Keeping kada and autobusas the same makes the direction of the journey the important difference.

steps.title: A bus platform
steps.note: Aikštelė is a bus-station platform here. Iš takes genitive: both trečia and aikštelė change to trečios aikštelės. You already used iš Kauno for a journey's origin.
